prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Forward, Together sets out Theresa May’s plan for strong and stable leadership to deliver a smooth, orderly Brexit and to tackle five giant, long‑term challenges: securing a strong economy, navigating Brexit and a changing world, healing enduring social divisions, responding to an ageing society, and harnessing fast‑changing technology. The manifesto pledges to govern from the mainstream—rejecting ideological extremes—using an active, accountable state to back enterprise, uphold fair markets, strengthen national security, and build a Great Meritocracy that works for ordinary, working families across every part of the United Kingdom.

Economy and industrial strategy: Restore fiscal credibility with a balanced budget by the middle of the next decade; keep taxes low (no VAT rise; higher personal allowances; corporation tax to 17%); simplify tax and reform business rates. Champion free trade with a new Trade Bill, Trade Commissioners and a reconvened Board of Trade. Update capitalism’s rules: raise the National Living Wage, protect gig‑economy workers, crack down on tax evasion, enforce responsible takeovers, curb excessive executive pay and give workers a voice in boardrooms. Drive a modern industrial strategy: lift R&D to the OECD average, deploy a £23bn National Productivity Investment Fund, create Future Britain funds, back SMEs, deliver sector deals, cheaper competitive energy, a diverse energy mix (global leadership in offshore wind) and a well‑regulated UK shale industry that shares benefits with local communities. Invest in HS2, Northern Powerhouse Rail, Heathrow expansion, roads, EVs and full‑fibre/5G.

Stronger communities and the Union: Spread opportunity through devolution, culture and infrastructure; support rural, coastal and farming communities; uphold animal welfare; lead a 25‑year environment plan. Strengthen the precious Union, oppose a second Scottish referendum now, and create a UK Shared Prosperity Fund as EU funds return.

Brexit and Global Britain: Leave the EU, single market and customs union; seek a deep and special partnership; end vast EU payments; convert EU law via a Great Repeal Bill; protect workers’ rights; maintain the Common Travel Area and Gibraltar’s rights; control immigration; and put the final deal to Parliament. Lead globally on free trade, climate, security and development (maintain 0.7% aid but spend it better). Meet NATO 2% with real annual increases; retain Trident; invest £178bn in equipment; back veterans. Strengthen policing, counter‑terror and cyber defences; streamline economic crime enforcement.

Democracy, justice and security: Votes for life, voter ID, complete the boundary review to 600 MPs, retain First Past the Post, repeal the Fixed‑term Parliaments Act. Put victims’ rights in law; reform prisons for safety, work and rehabilitation.

The Great Meritocracy: Expand good school places—more free schools, lift the ban on new selective schools with safeguards, require universities/independent schools to help run state schools; fairer funding with a £4bn rise; universal primary breakfasts; a knowledge‑rich curriculum and teacher support. Create world‑class technical education with T‑levels, Institutes of Technology, 3m high‑quality apprenticeships and lifelong retraining. Control and reduce net migration to sustainable levels; drive integration and confront extremism. Tackle burning injustices: close gender and ethnicity pay gaps, get 1m more disabled people into work, deliver a new Mental Health Act and services, and pass a landmark Domestic Violence and Abuse Bill. Halve rough sleeping by 2022.

Cost of living and housing: Enforce fair consumer markets (rail, telecoms, leasehold, rentals, whiplash, parking); cap poor‑value energy tariffs and roll out smart meters; upgrade fuel‑poor homes; introduce a “Breathing Space” scheme for debt. Build 1.5m homes by 2022 with higher standards, council and housing association delivery, modern methods, and fixed‑term social housing linked to a new Right to Buy.

Restoring the intergenerational contract: Maintain the Triple Lock to 2020 then a Double Lock; align state pension age with longevity. Secure sustainable social care—include housing wealth fairly with a £100k asset floor and deferred payments—and means‑test Winter Fuel Payments to fund health and care. Provide the NHS with at least £8bn more, more staff, modern buildings and technology, faster access to new treatments, seven‑day services and improved mental health, while charging fairly for non‑resident care.

A digital charter: Make the UK the best place to start and grow a digital business and the safest place online—full‑fibre and 5G, stronger data protection (including a right to delete data at 18), tougher platform responsibilities, digital government by default, a new geospatial data body, and a proportionate, ethical framework for data and online harms. Repeal Leveson 2 and Section 40 to uphold a free press.

This is a confident, pragmatic Conservative plan to unite the country and secure a stronger Britain and a prosperous future—forward, together.
